[spoiler=Part 2-The Night March][i]Part II (Theme Playing in Background:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LlgWqcHXD8w)

[u][b]Alexas Apartment | 7:02 AM[/b][/u]

Ash still drifts in the air outside. The city is silent, still haunted by last nights massacre.
 Inside, the apartment is quiet. The leopard girl, small and alert, stands at the window, tail still.
Alexa sits at the edge of the bed, his S.S.E. badge glinting faintly in his open palm.
He glances toward the girl.

[b]Alexa (gently)[/b]
Whats your name?

A long pause.
She hesitates.

[b]Leopard Girl (whispers)[/b]
My father used to say names are sacred. If you tell the wrong person, they can curse you.
Alexa nods, respectful.

[b]Alexa:[/b]
Then I wont ask again.
She studies him. Steps forward  slowly  and sits beside him, close but cautious.

[b]Leopard Girl:[/b]
...But if you promise not to curse me
 You can call me Luma.

Alexa looks at her  really looks. And, for the first time in days, he smiles.

[b]Alexa:[/b]
Luma.
 Thats a strong name.

[u][b]Oceanice S.S.E. HQ S.S.E. Command Room[/b][/u]
The lights are dim. The massive wall screens flicker between thermal footage and political broadcasts.
General Tassar, a broad-shouldered, silver-haired officer, stands in silence, watching a loop of last nights massacre. Protestors burning. Smoke. The lion activist's body twitchingthen still.

[b]General Tassar (grimly):[/b]
You shouldve let the dogs bite back first. Now we look like tyrants.

President Vanklyis Adelais Herman, seated by the glass wall overlooking the city, doesnt turn.

[b]President Vanklyis(calmly):[/b]
History isnt written by dogs.

He finishes the last sip of his bourbon, sets the glass down with a cold clink.

[b]President Herman (sharper):[/b]
Its written by survivors.

The doors open behind them.

Klaus Enters*
Klaus, the feline butler and intelligence assistant, enters with perfect poise, holding a silver datapad.

[b]Klaus:[/b]
My Führer. I apologize for the interruption but you should see this.
He walks toward the center screen and connects the feed.

[b]Klaus (softly):[/b]
Zserich News Broadcast just aired an urgent update. The world is already watching.

[u][b]Z.N.B. Broadcast  July 3, 2025 | Dalesburg, New Westmore[/b][/u]
The screen cuts to a solemn news anchor, surrounded by flickering candlelight.

[b]Anchor:[/b]
Breaking News: At midnight, President Holt of New Westmore was reported dead in a fatal car crashallegedly caused by drunk driving. Circumstances remain unclear, and officials in New Westmore have yet to release a full statement.
Clips of protests, candlelight vigils, and confusion flood the screen.

[b]Anchor continued*[/b]
In a surprising diplomatic turn, President Vanklyis Adelais Herman of the Oceanice Republic released the following public statement:

[b]President Vanklyis(recorded, formal)[/b]
Though our nations have often stood at odds diplomatically, I offer my deepest condolences to the people of New Westmore on the tragic passing of President Holt. A lifeany lifelost so suddenly is a loss for humanity. May his family find strength during this time, and may New Westmore find unity in the wake of this sorrow.

As a gesture of peace, the Oceanice Republic will suspend all military movements near shared maritime zones until further notice.

[u][b]Coastal Cliffs of Sevetrea  Later That Day[/b][/u]
Oceanice ceremonial guards line the cliffside in crisp dress uniforms. The wind howls. Artillery guns stand ready.
The Guard Commander, standing tall with a ceremonial saber, signals the salute.

[b]Commander (yelling):[/b]
FIRE!

The artillery echoes across the cliffs, one shot after anothersix in total.
As the smoke rises into the sky, the Guard lifts their right fists.

[b]All Guards (in unison):[/b]
Though divided by politics, we are united by honor.
 May President Holt find peace beyond the veil!

Two flags rise  the Oceanice Republic and New Westmore banners, side by side.
A rare image of solemn peace.

[u][b]Back to the Command Room  Private Reaction[/b][/u]
The video feed ends.

[b]General Tassar (sincerely):[/b]
A noble gesture, sir.

[b]President Herman (leaning back, smirking faintly):[/b]
Yes. Very noble.

He stands, brushing imaginary dust from his lapel.

[b]President Herman (coldly, to Klaus):[/b]
Such a waste of good bourbon to toast a drunk fools death.

[b]Klaus (stoic):[/b]
You seemed to speak kindly of him, sir.
[b]
President Vanklyis[/b]
Publicly, yes. But dont be mistaken, Klaus.

He turns to the glass, eyes watching the smoke trail from the Sevetrea coast.

[b]President Vanklyis(low, pleased):[/b]
New Westmore is in disarray. Their medias too distracted to paint us as monsters. Their parliament will flail without Holt.
 And while they weep, we move.

[b]General Tassar:[/b]
So the purge continues?

[b]President Vanklyis(nods):[/b]
We pause the blade  not to sheath it
 but to sharpen it.

General Tassar turns away from the display and folds his arms, expression unbothered.

[b]General Tassar (flatly):[/b]
He was just a drunk fool.

President Vanklyis steps closer to the window, watching the flags sway in the wind over Sevetrea.

[b]President Vanklyis(smirking)[/b]
Indeed. The man who tried to frighten us. To box us in with his treaties, threats, and empty sanctions.

He lifts the glass again  this time not in mourning, but mockery.

[b]President Vanklyis(cold, amused):[/b]
But in the end God plays in this world.

He downs the bourbon in one clean sip, then sets the glass down slowly.

[b]President Vanklyis(final)[/b]
So farewell, Mr. Holt.
 You were a pain in the sht* to us for far too long.

He turns his back to the window and walks toward the map table, showing man made island that was drawn out.

[b]President Vanklyis(sharper, with quiet disdain):[/b]
And now that Holts out of the way
 its time we redraw the map.

He taps the man-made island marked on the glowing table map.

[b]President Vanklyis (firm)[/b]
The seas will be ours. And the ULR are
 blinded, stumbling behind the smoke of their illusions.

He scoffs, walking slowly around the table.

[b]President Vanklyis(disgusted):[/b]
I never trusted them. All that talk about equality, about building a better world for humans and non-humans alike.
He pauses. His lip curls in contempt.

[b]President Herman (spitting the words):[/b]
A nation built by animals, led by fools
 And they thought wed kneel to them?

He lets out a dry, cruel laugh and raises his glass.

[b]President Vanklyis (coldly):[/b]
Clowns playing parliament.
 And while they grieve we build.

He downs the final sip of his bourbon, eyes glinting in the screens reflection.

[b]Klaus quietly, after Herman leaves*[/b]
May the world never see the man behind the mask.
He turns back to the screen, but his eyes linger longer on Lumas surveillance feed, tucked quietly into one corner.

[u][b]Alexas Apartment  Later That Morning[/b][/u]
Luma sat curled on the couch, legs tucked under her. She stared at the blank TV screen  not really watching, but hiding behind it.
Alexa stood by the kitchen counter, pouring hot water into two chipped mugs. One had faded flowers, the other a soldiers insignia.

[b]Alexa (softly):[/b]
Milk or sugar?

[b]Luma (barely audible):[/b]
Both.

He stirred the tea and walked it to her, placing the mug gently in her paws.

[b]Alexa:[/b]
Its not much but its warm.
She looked up at him with tired, unblinking eyes.

[b]Luma:[/b]
Why did you save me?

Alexa paused. He opened his mouth  then closed it.
He sat down beside her.

[b]Alexa:[/b]
Because I couldnt let another child die. Not again.

A long silence stretched between them.

[b]Luma (whispers):[/b]
Youre not like them.

[u][b]Alexas Apartment  Late Afternoon[/b][/u]

The apartment is quiet. Alexa and Luma sit at a small dinner table. A simple meal: rice, eggs, and tea. She eats carefully, her ears twitching with every clink of the fork. Alexa smiles gently.
Then
A sudden knock.
 No a thud.

Outside, S.S.E. guards step back as President Vanklyis Adelais Herman, dressed in his heavy black overcoat, storms into the hallway, face burning with fury.

[b]Vanklyis:[/b]
Where is he?

[b]Guard:[/b]
Room 92D, sir. Apartment wing East.

[b]Vanklyis:[/b]
He dares ignore my calls?

He slams open the apartment door without waiting for permission.

[u][b]Inside the Apartment[/b][/u]
The door crashes open. Alexa leaps to his feet. Luma gasps and pulls behind him.

[b]Alexa:[/b]
F-Father?!

[b]Vanklyis (voice shaking):[/b]
You dont answer my calls. You vanish. Then I find you herewith one of them?

His eyes meet Lumas. The air falls still.

She looks up at him, trembling. But something about hersomething in her eyesfreezes him in place.
His rage collapses into silence.

[u][b]Flashback[/b][/u]

A candle-lit dining room.

 Vanklyis, younger, smiling beside a woman and three children.

 The daughter  maybe five years old  has the same eyes as Luma.

 She offers her father a spoonful of soup, giggling.

 His wife brushes her hair back. His sons laugh.

 Then, the image flickers 

 The girl coughs, her hands weak

 Her hospital bed. Her fading voice.

 His tears. Her death.

[u][b]Back to Present[/b][/u]

Vanklyis steps back, eyes wet.

[b]Vanklyis (quiet, broken):[/b]
I had a daughter. Before all this madness. You remind me of her.

Luma doesnt speak. She peeks out from behind Alexa, tail twitching nervously.
Vanklyis kneels slowly and  to Alexas shock  offers a nod.

[b]Vanklyis (cold but composed):[/b]
Youre welcome to be part of this family, girl. But only if you listen. Obey.
He stands up.

[b]Vanklyis (to the hallway):[/b]
Klaus!

A tall furry cat-servant, well-groomed in a black uniform, steps in with a bow.

[b]Vanklyis:[/b]
She is to be protected. Watched. Fed. No one touches her. If anyone from the S.S.E. questions itrefer them to me.

[b]Klaus:[/b]
Yes, my Führer.

Vanklyis grabs Alexa by the shoulder and pulls him into the hallway.

[u][b]Private Study Room  Door Closes Behind[/b][/u]

[b]Vanklyis (exploding):[/b]
So you bring this poor furry to your house?! WHAT WERE YOU THINKING?!

[b]Alexa:[/b]
I was thinking like a human. Not a machine.

[b]Vanklyis:[/b]
How did I raise a son like this? A son who eats dinner with the very beasts we are at war with! I am the Führer of this nation, Alexa. What do you think people will say when they see us babysitting an animal?!

[b]Alexa (calmly):[/b]
Theyll say we still have a soul.
 Or maybe theyll say we remember what it means to lose a child.

Vanklyis stares at him. Breathing heavy. Silent*

[b]Alexa (firm):[/b]
She doesnt pose a threat. Shes just a girl.
 Let me take her to Berlinwerk. Give her peace. Shes lost everything.

A long pause*

[b]Vanklyis (quietly):[/b]
You always knew how to twist words like your mother

He walks to the window*

[b]Vanklyis (cold but subdued):[/b]
Fine. You may adopt the girl. But if she becomes a problemI end it myself. Understood?

[b]Alexa (nods):[/b]
Understood.

Vanklyis finishes packing. His convoy prepares to depart.

[b]Vanklyis:[/b]
I'm leaving for Valsune City in Lonaco. Meeting with the President of the United Lavian Republic. International pressure grows We must not show weakness.
He turns to Alexa and Luma, now dressed for travel.

[b]Vanklyis:[/b]
Ive arranged for both of you to be sent to the private estate in Berlinwerk, deep within the wooden lands. Few know it exists. Theres a palace there  the home of our founders. You'll be safe.
He hesitates, then softens.

[b]Vanklyis:[/b]
Before I leave, I want a dinner. The three of us. Just once more.
Luma looks up at him. Unsure. Still afraid.
But she nods.

Part 3...

His rage collapses into silence.

[u][b]Flashback[/b][/u]

A candle-lit dining room.

 Vanklyis, younger, smiling beside a woman and three children.

 The daughter  maybe five years old  has the same eyes as Luma.

 She offers her father a spoonful of soup, giggling.

 His wife brushes her hair back. His sons laugh.

 Then, the image flickers 

 The girl coughs, her hands weak

 Her hospital bed. Her fading voice.

 His tears. Her death.

Vanklyis steps back, eyes wet.

[b]Vanklyis (quiet, broken):[/b]
I had a daughter. Before all this madness. You remind me of her.

[b]Vanklyis (cold but composed):[/b]
Youre welcome to be part of this family, girl. But only if you listen. Obey.

[b]Vanklyis (to the hallway):[/b]

[b]Vanklyis:[/b]

[b]Klaus:[/b]

[b]Alexa:[/b]

[b]Vanklyis:[/b]

[b]Alexa (calmly):[/b]
Theyll say we still have a soul.
 Or maybe theyll say we remember what it means to lose a child.

Vanklyis stares at him. Breathing heavy. Silent*

[b]Alexa (firm):[/b]
She doesnt pose a threat. Shes just a girl.
 Let me take her to Berlinwerk. Give her peace. Shes lost everything.

A long pause*

[b]Vanklyis (quietly):[/b]
You always knew how to twist words like your mother

He walks to the window*

[b]Vanklyis (cold but subdued):[/b]
Fine. You may adopt the girl. But if she becomes a problemI end it myself. Understood?

[b]Alexa (nods):[/b]
Understood.

Vanklyis finishes packing. His convoy prepares to depart.

[b]Vanklyis:[/b]
I'm leaving for Valsune City in Lonaco. Meeting with the President of the United Lavian Republic. International pressure grows We must not show weakness.

[b]Vanklyis:[/b]
Ive arranged for both of you to be sent to the private estate in Berlinwerk, deep within the wooden lands. Few know it exists. Theres a palace there  the home of our founders. You'll be safe.
